mechanicTruth: Air pressure falls as air cools, so about one PSI leaves a tire for every ten degrees Fahrenheit the temperature drops - which is why the low-pressure light appears after the first cold night with nothing punctured, and why the reading only means something taken cold, before driving warms the tires and reads high.
selectedCaption: You didn't run over anything. That warning light isn't damage — it's the weather. Every ten degrees the temperature drops pulls about one PSI out of every tire. That's why the light shows up on the first cold Cleveland morning, out of nowhere. Warm tires read high and hide the real number. Check the pressure cold, before you drive. Worth checking before that first frost.
voiceoverScript: You did not run over anything - the first cold snap does this. Cooling air shrinks, so tire pressure falls. About a pound for every ten degrees. Read them cold, before you drive. One clue worth checking, not a verdict.
